Issued at 249 AM EST Sun Nov 22 2026

- Rain Showers This Afternoon

Upper troughing and the right entrance region of an upper jet core
is moving into Wisconsin this morning with rain showers along and
ahead of a surface cold front. Temperatures ahead of the front in
our region (prior to mid afternoon) should reach the upper 50s to
mid 60s. Rain showers and the quick progression of the cold front
should drop temperatures into the 40s by late afternoon or
evening. A decrease in cloud cover overnight along with CAA
overspreading the region (ie. 850mb temperatures dipping down into
the -5C to -8C range by Monday morning) should allow for lows 
Monday morning to bottom out around or below freezing across
central Lower MI.

- Brief Period of Light Snow Showers Monday

Still looking like a narrow window for some light snow showers
Monday afternoon into early Monday night as the upper trough axis
swings over Lake Michigan around 21z Monday and 850mb temperatures
continuing dropping to -10C. GFS and RRFS Bufkit soundings for LDM
support snow with a saturated DGZ and a bit better moisture
profile shown in the 1000-850mb layer compared to earlier data with
80-90% RH forecast. However, this window appears to be around 6
hours or less. Brief, light snow accumulations are possible
especially after dark across the US 10 corridor and locations
north of Muskegon along the lakeshore. Pavement temperatures may
be a touch too warm for much in the way of slippery roads.

- Growing Likelihood for Rain and Snow for the Holiday Period

It is now appearing more likely that Michigan will be impacted by
a storm system for the Thanksgiving holiday period. A growing
ensemble membership is indicating higher precipitation potential
compared to past runs. The ensemble mean 500mb height pattern from
the ECE/GEFS/CMC all show a closed upper low positioned W to SW 
of Lower Michigan by 12z Thursday along with a negatively tilted 
trough extending from it in a NW to SE fashion. In spite of model 
guidance strongly favoring a Nor'easter development on 
Thanksgiving with potentially significant holiday impacts across 
the Mid Atlantic and Northeast, this type of upper level pattern 
across the Great Lakes favors a quasi-phasing of our upper pattern
with the deepening East Coast trough and surface low. The net 
effect of this will be to push the western reaches of the surface
low into the Great Lakes, leading to both rain and snow chances 
for the holiday period.

The 50th percentile for the 24hr ensemble QPF Thursday into Friday
indicates a range of 0.25"-0.50" while 75th percentile QPF pushes
toward 0.75". NBM pops are currently 50-60% on Thanksgiving but
that will likely be trending up. This event could play out in a
variety of ways depending on precipitation timing and whether the
atmospheric thermal profiles cool sufficiently enough to turn
precipitation over to snow. Initially the model soundings would
suggest rain as the dominant p-type on Thursday but a rain/snow
mix or just wet snow could occur during the morning hours before
changing to liquid. 

Thanksgiving night into Friday, a period of wet snow may occur 
once again and there is a risk for accumulations. ECE 50th 
percentile 24hr snow on Friday indicates generally less than 1" 
though 75th percentile snow jumps into the 2"-4" range. However, 
with ensemble mean highs around 40 (as well as NBM), the consensus
is not quite there yet for snow that would stick. Web bulb 
effects congruent with heavier snowfall rates could certainly take
over and turn this into an interesting event, but not confident 
yet. It is noted that the 00z deterministic ECMWF soundings are 
nearly entirely below freezing on Friday with snow as the dominant
p-type, and it certainly is swinging for the fences on snow 
accumulations. But for that scenario to pan out, things would have
to come together perfectly. Ensemble guidance is the way to go at
this point and we have time to watch this evolve. The bottom line
is to at least be aware that winter impacts are possible over the
holiday period but temperatures may be a bit too warm for 
substantial impacts at this point, subject to change as model
guidance better handles this system.
